theater: 西安納托利亞米利都與薩迪斯

battle.name: 波斯起義
battle.theater: 西安納托利亞米利都與薩迪斯
battle.brief: 公元前553年，伊奧尼亞城邦聯軍與西部諸省總督同時起兵，米利都的阿里斯塔戈拉奪城自立，552年拉比蘭圖斯會戰聯軍擊潰波斯大軍，545年拉德海戰失利後米利都陷落。卡面的埃及月牙劍是青銅時代的舊式彎刃，早已退出軍列，戰陣上起作用的是波斯人的弓陣、戰斧與短刀。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場起義有兩個同時燃起又互相呼應的戰場。西部是伊奧尼亞與卡里亞的城邦聯軍：米利都、以弗所、科斯、普里埃涅、萊斯博斯、薩摩斯等十二座城邦先後加入，聯軍以米利都的阿里斯塔戈拉與希斯提亞斯為核心，兵種以重裝步兵方陣為骨幹，配各城的輕裝步兵、弓箭手與為數不多的騎兵。東部是帝國總督們的起兵：呂底亞、卡帕多細亞與薩迪斯周邊的波斯總督與地方貴族各自舉兵，帶著直屬部隊與徵召的民兵，兩股叛軍在同一條線上策應，使大流士一世一度只能靠王宮近衛的精銳步兵維持局面。波斯方面的軍隊由薩迪斯的總督節度，呂底亞的步兵與弓手、卡帕多細亞的騎兵、塞薩利亞與小亞細亞的徵召兵依次開拔，海軍則由腓尼基、塞浦路斯與呂基亞的船匠和水手組成，經驗遠勝對手的伊奧尼亞船員。第三方各有算盤：呂基亞與塞浦路斯被強徵船隻，只求保住自己的商路；斯巴達與雅典在起義初期按兵不動，直到米利都陷落、求援的消息東渡之後才改變態度；色雷斯的王公則被捲入追捕阿里斯塔戈拉的行動。整場衝突沒有外國遠征軍介入，全部戰鬥都發生在安納托利亞西部與帝國腹地的行省線上。
countriesEn: This revolt had two theatres that flared up at the same time and answered one another. In the west was the league of the Ionian and Carian city-states: Miletus, Ephesus, Cos, Priene, Lesbos, Samos and the other cities of the Ionian alliance joined in turn, with the heart of the league in Aristagoras and Histiaeus of Miletus; its fighting core was the phalanx of heavy infantry, supported by the light infantry, the archers and the very small cavalry numbers each city could supply. In the east was the rising of the satraps: the Persian satraps and local notables of Lydia, Cappadocia and the districts around Sardis each rose with their own retainers and with levied militia, and the two rebel currents reinforced one another along the same front, so that Darius I could for a time hold his position with nothing more than the picked foot of the palace guard. The Persian army was directed from Sardis: Lydian foot and archers, Cappadocian cavalry, and levies from Cilicia and the Lesser Phrygia moved out in turn, while the navy was built up from Phoenician, Cypriot and Lycian shipwrights and crews, whose experience far exceeded that of the Ionian sailors. The third parties followed their own interest: Lycia and Cyprus had their ships requisitioned and cared chiefly for their own trade routes; Sparta and Athens stood still in the first months of the revolt and only changed their posture after the fall of Miletus and the arrival of the appeal across the sea; and the Thracian princes were drawn into the manhunt for Aristagoras. No foreign expeditionary force entered the fighting at any point: every engagement took place along the line between western Anatolia and the satrapies of the imperial interior.
people: 起義軍方面留下姓名的關鍵人物不多，但每一個都改變了戰局。阿里斯塔戈拉是米利都的統治者、赫卡托姆諾斯之子，他靠大流士的信任取得對城邦的支配，起事後立即奪取城內權力，清除反對他的勢力，把財物分給部眾，再以使者把起兵的消息帶到伊奧尼亞各城，並把黑海沿岸的殖民地當作退路。真正把火種點著的是他的親戚希斯提亞斯：這位米利都貴族在大流士宮廷中任職，往返於波斯與米利都之間，說服宮廷先撤走駐米利都的波斯守軍，又策動阿里斯塔戈拉動手，後來又帶著聯軍回到米利都主持城防。包圍米利都的圍城戰中，希斯提亞斯指揮城內守軍抵抗到底，城破被俘，在押往薩迪斯的路上企圖自殺未成，被帶到總督面前後才被處死；死前他托人給雅典人送去一封信，訴說波斯人如何對待受苦的伊奧尼亞人，這封信直接催生了前499年的伊奧尼亞起義。阿里斯塔戈拉的兄弟歐邁爾統率伊奧尼亞艦隊，在拉德海戰中指揮分列兩翼的戰列，最後被波斯人逐個擊破。波斯方面的主宰是大流士一世，他先後派遣奧塔涅斯、法爾納刻斯與麥加比茲率軍平叛；米利都陷落後，阿塔弗內斯奉命出任薩迪斯總督，長期處理伊奧尼亞的善後，隨行的麥加比茲後來也獲授總督權柄。拉比蘭圖斯會戰中扭轉戰局的是卡里亞的步兵與首領，他們在平原上拖住了波斯縱隊，使聯軍得以合圍。
peopleEn: Few leaders of the insurgents are named in the sources, but every one of them changed the course of the war. Aristagoras was the ruler of Miletus, the son of Hecatomnus; it was Darius's trust that gave him his grip on the city, and once the revolt was launched he seized power inside the walls at once, removed the faction opposed to him, distributed property to his followers, and then sent envoys to the Ionian cities with the news of the rising, while looking to his Black Sea colonies as a place of retreat. The spark was really lit by his kinsman Histiaeus: this Milesian aristocrat held office at the court of Darius and travelled between Persia and Miletus, persuading the court to withdraw the Persian garrison from the city first, and then pressing Aristagoras to move; later he returned with the league to Miletus and took charge of its defence. In the siege of Miletus, Histiaeus directed the resistance of the garrison to the end; the city fell and he was taken prisoner, and on the road to Sardis he attempted to kill himself without success, being brought before the satrap and put to death there. Before his death he had a letter carried to the Athenians, describing how the Persians had treated the sufferers of Ionia, and that letter directly produced the Ionian revolt of 499 BC. Omer, the brother of Aristagoras, commanded the Ionian fleet and directed the battle line formed in two wings at Lade, where the Persian ships were picked off one by one. On the Persian side the master of events was Darius I, who sent Otanes, Pharnaces and Megabyzus with armies against the rebels in turn; after the fall of Miletus, Artaphernes was appointed satrap at Sardis to handle the aftermath in Ionia for years to come, and Megabyzus travelling with him was likewise granted satrapal authority. The men who turned the Battle of the Labyrinth were the Carian foot and their commanders, who held the Persian columns in the plain and so allowed the league to close around them.
kits: 卡面兵器是「埃及月牙劍」：青銅時代的埃及外彎單刃劍，砍進去不必拔出，比直劍更早出現。這件兵器比這場起義早了三千年有奇，到前553年早已退出歐亞軍列，並沒有出現在米利都或拉比蘭圖斯的戰場上；把它放進來，是因為它標示出冷兵器中「單刃彎曲、專供劈砍」這一技術譜系的源頭，而波斯軍中與它功能相對應的，正是那種不用刺、只管砍的戰斧。阿契美尼德步兵的標準裝備是：身披魚鱗或皮革鑲片的小鎧，戴有護頰的青銅或鐵盔，手持短矛或標槍，配一面以藤條編骨架、外蒙牛皮的波斯大盾，盾面常釘金屬盾鈕；弓手用角與木製的複合弓，箭袋懸於腰際，箭鏃分金屬三棱與倒鉤兩種。切割用的兵器是雙刃的「薩加里斯」戰斧與短小的「阿基那克斯」短刀，後者連鞘佩在腰側，是波斯貴族與軍官最常被刻上浮雕的兵器。伊奧尼亞與卡里亞的聯軍則是希臘式裝備：青銅頭盔、脛甲、以亞麻或皮製的護胸，一面覆皮的重圓盾，長矛與短劍；卡里亞人另以小型圓盾、標槍與擲石兵著稱，善於在兩翼游鬥。攻城方面，波斯人在米利都城外挖壕築土壘，把城牆包成孤立的一段；海戰方面，伊奧尼亞人用上自己建造的三列槳戰船與各城邦湊出的運兵船，並靠漁船與商船在岸邊接應。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh: an outward-curving single-edged sword of the Bronze Age, which did not have to be pulled back out after a cut and which appeared earlier than the straight sword. This weapon predates the revolt by more than three thousand years and had long since left the armies of Eurasia by 553 BC; it certainly never appeared at Miletus or on the field of the Labyrinth. It is placed here because it marks the fountainhead of that family of cold weapons which is single-edged, curved and made for chopping, and the Persian counterpart of it in function is exactly the battle-axe, the weapon that cuts without stabbing. The standard equipment of the Achaemenid foot was a small corselet of scaled or leather-plated construction, a bronze or iron helmet with cheek pieces, a short spear or javelin, and a large Persian wicker shield with a leather covering and often a metal boss; the archers used composite bows of horn and wood, with the quiver worn at the hip, and their arrow-heads came in two kinds, a metal three-edged head and a barbed head. The cutting weapons were the double-edged sagaris axe and the short akinakes, which was carried at the side in its scabbard and which is the arm most often cut in relief on Persian nobles and officers. The Ionian and Carian league, by contrast, used Greek equipment: bronze helmets, greaves, a cuirass of linen or leather, a heavy round shield with a leather facing, the long spear and the short sword. The Carians were further noted for small round shields, javelins and slingers, and were good at skirmishing on the flanks. On the siege side the Persians dug a ditch and raised earthen works outside Miletus so as to isolate a section of the wall; on the naval side the Ionians put to use the triremes they had built themselves together with troop transports scraped up from the cities, while fishing boats and merchantmen lay in close along the shore to give support.
tactics: 聯軍的戰法建立在希臘城邦的成熟經驗上：重裝步兵列成密集方陣，盾牌互相搭接向前推進，矛尖越過前排肩頭，逼迫波斯縱隊在狹窄地形上失去展開的空間；卡里亞的輕裝步兵與弓箭手不斷從兩側擾亂，邊打邊退，把波斯人拖進被費達斯河汊道切割的沼澤地帶，這正是拉比蘭圖斯一戰得名的來由——會戰中聯軍先用卡里亞人拖住波斯主力，再以方陣反擊，把退路封死，聯軍獲勝。伊奧尼亞人接著轉向海防：在米利都近海集結約一百二十艘戰列船，試圖靠船數與船質封住波斯援軍的航路，並把卡里亞與呂基亞的援艦編入兩翼。包圍米利都的波斯軍在做法上完全相反：先以大軍合圍，再沿城牆挖壕、堆土築起壘牆，企圖在陸地上一舉耗盡守軍；圍城同時用海軍封住港口，斷絕城內的援兵與糧食。拉德海戰是全戰役最關鍵的一次海戰，波斯艦隊利用船多、划槌好、弓箭手多的優勢試圖包抄，伊奧尼亞聯軍排成縱列硬撐住正面，但薩摩斯與萊斯博斯的船隊先後離陣，陣線一散即全線崩潰。聯軍的致命弱點是各自為政：城邦之間沒有可靠的統一指揮，撤退時也沒有共同掩護，結果被逐個殲滅。
tacticsEn: The tactics of the league rested on the settled experience of the Greek city-states: heavy infantry stood in a dense phalanx, shields overlapped as they advanced, spear-points cleared the shoulders of the front rank, and the Persian columns were forced to give up the room they needed to deploy in narrow ground; Carian light infantry and archers harassed from both flanks, striking and withdrawing, dragging the Persians into the marshy ground cut up by the branches of the Maeander, and that is precisely where the Battle of the Labyrinth got its name: in the engagement the league first used the Carians to hold the Persian main force, then counter-attacked with the phalanx and sealed the retreat, and the league won. The Ionians then turned to sea defence: about a hundred and twenty warships were mustered off Miletus to seal the route of Persian reinforcement by strength of numbers and of hull, with Carian and Lycian contingents worked into the two wings. The Persian army besieging Miletus proceeded on exactly the opposite logic: it invested the city with the mass of the army first, then dug a ditch along the wall and heaped up earth into a rampart, seeking to wear the garrison out by land in one stroke; the sea force closed the port at the same time, cutting off both reinforcement and grain. The Battle of Lade was the most decisive action of the whole war at sea. The Persian fleet used its advantages in the number of ships, in the quality of the oars and in the number of archers to try to turn the Ionians; the league formed line and held the front, but the contingents of Samos and of Lesbos left the line in turn, and once the formation was broken the whole line collapsed. The fatal weakness of the league was its lack of unity: there was no reliable common command between the cities and no mutual covering on the withdrawal, and the squadrons were destroyed one after another.
data: 可核實的數字不多，以下幾組較為可靠。起義始於公元前553年，552年在馬安德河下游平原爆發拉比蘭圖斯會戰，帝國東部的總督起義則在550年前後被壓平，米利都陷落在545年（亦有記為546年），海上的拉德海戰緊接其後，兩役相隔不過一年。聯軍的海上兵力在拉德海戰有明確記載：伊奧尼亞方面出動約一百二十艘戰列船，波斯方面主力艦數與之相當，另配數百艘運輸與輔助船，海軍的差距主要體現在乘員與經驗上，而非船殼數量。伊奧尼亞聯盟的城邦一般認為有十二座，主要城邦在米利都、以弗所、科斯、普里埃涅、萊斯博斯、薩摩斯與福卡亞等地，城市間距離多在數十至一百公里之間，同一支艦隊可在數日內往返。地理上，薩迪斯至米利都的陸路約一百五十公里，途中要穿越內弗薩河谷與數處山口；拉比蘭圖斯會戰的戰場在馬安德河下游、費達斯河汊道縱橫的沖積平原上，退路容易迷失，正是決定勝負的地形。波斯方面的軍隊總數沒有可靠記載，古代作者多以「極大」形容；希羅多德為大流士後來遠征希臘寫下八十萬大軍的數字，歷來被學界視為誇大之辭，不宜直接套用到這場內戰。最後一個可以量化的後果是人口的遷徙：米利都陷落後，大批米利都人遷往黑海沿岸的殖民地重建居所，其中一部分在數十年後成為波斯再度用兵時的立足點。
dataEn: Only a limited number of figures can be verified, and the following groups are the most reliable. The revolt began in 553 BC; the Battle of the Labyrinth was fought in 552 BC on the plain below the Maeander; the rising of the satraps in the interior of the empire was crushed around 550 BC; the fall of Miletus came in 545 BC, though some accounts give 546, and the naval Battle of Lade followed immediately after, the two engagements being no more than a year apart. The strength of the league at sea is explicitly recorded for Lade: the Ionians put out about a hundred and twenty warships, and the Persians matched them in the number of capital ships while adding several hundred transports and auxiliaries, the difference between the two navies lying mainly in the crews and their experience rather than in the number of hulls. The Ionian alliance is generally reckoned to have had twelve cities, the principal ones being Miletus, Ephesus, Cos, Priene, Lesbos, Samos and Phocaea, most of them from tens to a hundred kilometres apart, so that a single squadron could move between them in the space of a few days. Geographically, the land road from Sardis to Miletus is about a hundred and fifty kilometres and passes through the valley of the Hermus and several defiles; the field of the Battle of the Labyrinth lay on the alluvial plain below the Maeander, where the branches of the Maeander cut the ground in every direction and make a retreat easy to lose, and that terrain decided the engagement. There is no reliable figure for the size of the Persian army; the ancient writers generally content themselves with saying that it was very great. Herodotus gives eight hundred thousand for the later expedition of Darius into Greece, a number long treated by scholars as an exaggeration and one that should not be applied directly to this civil war. The last consequence that can be measured is the movement of people: after Miletus fell, a large number of Milesians were moved to the colonies on the Black Sea to rebuild their homes, and some of those settlements served decades later as the footholds from which Persia campaigned again.
cause: 起義的直接導火線來自波斯朝廷內部的一次密謀。伊奧尼亞城邦自前499年之後便處在波斯委任的「僭主」統治之下，米利都的阿里斯塔戈拉是靠大流士的信任才坐穩城邦首腦的地位，而宮廷重臣希斯提亞斯則希望借一次成功的冒險重新取得朝廷的青睞。二人商定：先由阿里斯塔戈拉以「波斯人要沒收沿岸耕地」為由起事，把薩迪斯的波斯守軍引出米利都；守軍一撤，希斯提亞斯便挾持米利都與其他城邦叛離。計劃進行得比預期更順利：守軍被騙走，兩人奪城自立，消息隨即傳遍伊奧尼亞。更深一層的原因是制度性的：卡爾一門在帝國西部的實力與自主性遠超安納托利亞其他行省，薩迪斯的總督握有兵權、財權與徵稅權，連駐軍調度都可以與宮廷討價還價；大流士自前522年清理魔僧篡位與諸省叛亂之後，亟需證明自己對西部行省的掌控力，而伊奧尼亞城邦的希臘式自治傳統、徵召希臘傭兵的開支、以及越來越重的貢賦，都讓雙方都相信對方不會先讓步。外部條件同樣重要：呂底亞、卡帕多細亞等地的總督因不滿朝廷而各自舉兵，把西部行省拖入全面內戰；前500年代波斯在希臘世界屢遭挫敗的消息，又給了伊奧尼亞人獨立的念頭。
causeEn: The immediate spark came from a plot inside the Persian court. Since 499 BC the Ionian cities had been ruled by tyrants appointed from Persia; Aristagoras of Miletus held his position at the head of his city through the trust of Darius, while Histiaeus, a weighty figure at court, hoped to recover his standing with the court through one successful gamble. The two worked out a plan between them: Aristagoras was to rise on the pretext that the Persians meant to confiscate the coastal farmland, and so draw the Persian garrison out of Miletus; once the garrison had withdrawn, Histiaeus was to take Miletus and the other cities with him out of Persian hands. The plan went even better than expected: the garrison was tricked out, the two seized the city, and the news spread through Ionia at once. The deeper cause was institutional. The satraps of the western empire held far more real power and independence than the governors of the other Anatolian provinces: the satrap at Sardis commanded the troops, the finances and the taxes, and could even bargain with the court over the disposition of the garrisons. Since Darius had settled the magian usurpation and the provincial revolts in 522 BC, he had every reason to demonstrate that his grip on the western provinces was real, and the Greek habit of self-government in the Ionian cities, the cost of hiring Greek mercenaries and the steadily increasing tribute all left both sides convinced that the other would not give way first. The external conditions mattered as much: satraps in Lydia, Cappadocia and elsewhere rose in their own grievance against the court and dragged the western provinces into a general civil war, and the news of Persian disappointments in the Greek world during the early fifth century BC gave the Ionians a new appetite for independence.
impact: 起義雖然失敗，但它改寫了波斯對西部邊疆的治理方式，也把一條新的因果鏈接進了後來兩百年的希臘世界。其一，聯軍的失敗讓大流士一世確認伊奧尼亞的城邦不能照舊由本地僭主把持：米利都陷落後，薩迪斯成為帝國在安納托利亞的實際指揮中心，阿塔弗內斯以總督身份常駐，稅收與兵役改由總督直轄，十二座城邦被要求按新的貢賦名目繳付；城邦的城牆被拆、艦隊被收編、人員被分批遷往黑海殖民地，城市的自主制度基本解體。其二，聯軍的失敗沒有消除希斯提亞斯留下的那封信帶來的政治效應：前499年伊奧尼亞再度起兵，前490年波斯的希臘遠征在馬拉松折戟，前480年薛西斯再率大軍西征，最終在薩拉米斯與普拉提亞折戟，波斯戰爭由此全面爆發，而起義的記憶正是後來希臘城邦抵抗波斯的士氣來源之一。其三，戰役在技術上留下兩項可見的後果：波斯海軍在拉德海戰中吃虧後更加倚重腓尼基與塞浦路斯的水手與船匠，希臘城邦則在敗績中體會到聯合艦隊需要統一指揮；福卡亞人西遷，把希臘城邦的殖民網推到大西洋岸的馬西利亞，成為後來希臘文明西進的踏腳石。其四，在武器史的層面上，這場戰爭把希臘重裝步兵方陣與波斯弓陣、藤盾、戰斧在同一片平原上並排擺開，其勝負不取決於個人武藝，而取決於投射火力、盾牌防禦與地形利用的配合，這正是後來希臘城邦在裝備上拼命追趕的差距所在。
impactEn: The revolt failed, but it rewrote the way Persia governed its western frontier and it spliced a new chain of cause and effect into the Greek world of the two centuries that followed. First, the defeat of the league convinced Darius I that the Ionian cities could not continue to be held by local tyrants: after the fall of Miletus, Sardis became the effective command centre of the empire in Anatolia, Artaphernes sat there permanently as satrap, taxation and military service passed directly to the satrap, and the twelve cities were called upon to pay under new headings of tribute; their walls were dismantled, their fleets taken into the Persian service, and their people moved off in batches to the Black Sea colonies, so that the autonomous institutions of the cities were broken up. Second, the defeat of the league did not cancel the political effect of the letter Histiaeus left behind: Ionia rose again in 499 BC, the Persian expedition into Greece broke itself at Marathon in 490 BC, and Xerxes came west with a great army in 480 BC to be broken in his turn at Salamis and Plataea, so that the Persian Wars opened in full, and the memory of the revolt was one of the sources of the morale with which the Greek cities later faced the Persians. Third, the war left two visible technical consequences: the Persian navy, having been worsted at Lade, relied all the more on Phoenician and Cypriot crews and shipwrights, while the Greek cities learned from their defeat that a combined fleet needed a single command; and the Phocaeans, migrating west, pushed the network of Greek colonies to Massalia on the shore of the Atlantic, which became a stepping-stone for the later westward reach of Greek civilisation. Fourth, at the level of the history of weapons, this war set the Greek phalanx of heavy infantry beside the Persian archers, wicker shields and battle-axes on the same plain, and the outcome turned not on individual valour but on the combination of missile fire, shield defence and use of the ground, which was precisely the gap the Greek cities afterwards laboured to close in their own equipment.
result: 公元前545年，米利都陷落，這場起義走到盡頭。拉比蘭圖斯會戰與薩迪斯周邊的總督起義在550年前後先後被平定：西部的伊奧尼亞聯軍在保住米利都與卡里亞之後轉入海上守勢；包圍米利都的波斯大軍在城北挖壕築壘，並以海軍封住港口，糧食與援兵一齊斷絕，城內守軍在反覆出擊中耗盡，該城最終被攻破。城破之後，聯軍殘部向西與向北潰散，歐邁爾的艦隊在拉德海戰被全殲，阿里斯塔戈拉退入色雷斯仍被追捕並殺死；希斯提亞斯在薩迪斯被處死，但他在死前送出的那封信已經上路。福卡亞人放棄城邑，渡海遷往伊比利亞與高盧海岸，與同族匯合；科斯、萊斯博斯、薩摩斯等城按條件投降，割讓船隻並繳納金錢，保留了城邦的形式。戰後大流士把伊奧尼亞直接置於薩迪斯總督的轄下，重編了行省的稅制與兵役，並把西部的失敗寫進了後來遠征希臘的計劃：前490年的馬拉松出師，名義上是要懲罰伊奧尼亞的背叛。對起義者而言，他們沒有得到國家，只留下了反覆被引用的一句求援；對波斯而言，邊疆倒是被壓住了，但西線的裂痕並未癒合，反而在二十餘年後以更大規模的戰爭重新爆發。
resultEn: In 545 BC Miletus fell and the revolt came to its end. The Battle of the Labyrinth and the rising of the satraps around Sardis were settled one after the other around 550 BC: the Ionian league in the west, having preserved Miletus and Caria, turned to a defensive posture at sea, while the great Persian army that invested Miletus dug its ditch and raised its earthen rampart on the north side of the city and sealed the port with the fleet, cutting off grain and reinforcement alike; the garrison was worn down by repeated sorties and the city was at last taken by assault. After the breach the remnants of the league scattered west and north, Omer's squadron was destroyed in the Battle of Lade, and Aristagoras, who withdrew into Thrace, was hunted down and killed; Histiaeus was put to death at Sardis, but the letter he sent before his death was already on its way. The Phocaeans gave up their city and crossed the sea to the coast of Iberia and Gaul, joining their kinsmen there; Cos, Lesbos, Samos and the other cities surrendered on terms, giving up ships and paying money, and so kept the outward form of their polities. After the war Darius put Ionia directly under the satrap at Sardis, reorganised the taxation and the military service of the provinces, and wrote the failure in the west into the plan for the later expedition into Greece: the march on Marathon in 490 BC was in its stated terms a punishment for the treachery of Ionia. For the insurgents there was no state at the end, only an appeal that was quoted again and again; for Persia the frontier was held, but the crack in the western line did not heal and broke open once more, on a far greater scale, a little more than two decades later.
